name: uriparser query string dissection (and compose round-trip)
description:
This feature parses a raw query string (the part of a URI after '?', untrusted input coming straight from a URL) into a linked list of key/value pairs, splitting on '&' and '=', percent-decoding (unescaping %XX sequences) and optionally turning '+' into ' ' and normalizing line breaks for each key and value. Because it walks attacker-controlled bytes, tracks overlapping key/value boundaries across repeated '&'/'=' characters, and performs dynamic allocation/unescaping per field, it is a prime target for off-by-one, integer-overflow and memory-corruption bugs.
- uriDissectQueryMallocA: target; core: DissectQueryMallocExMm -> AppendQueryItem -> UnescapeInPlaceEx
- uriDissectQueryMallocExA: variant (adds explicit plusToSpace/breakConversion parameters), same core as target
- uriDissectQueryMallocExMmA: variant (adds a custom UriMemoryManager so malloc/calloc/free failures in AppendQueryItem can be forced), same core as target, additionally exercises the memory-manager failure paths inside AppendQueryItem
- uriComposeQueryA / uriComposeQueryExA / uriComposeQueryMallocA / uriComposeQueryMallocExA / uriComposeQueryMallocExMmA: consumer/inverse operation — takes the UriQueryList produced by the dissect call and serializes it back to a query string (re-escaping, re-inserting '&'/'=' and optionally '+'<->' ' and CR/LF normalization), exercising ComposeQueryEngine/ComposeQueryCharsRequiredEx which is the natural round-trip check for the dissected data
- uriFreeQueryListA / uriFreeQueryListMmA: lifecycle cleanup of the list built by DissectQueryMalloc, needed to free the allocations made by AppendQueryItem
The input space to vary across C: the raw query bytes themselves (empty keys/values, repeated '&' and '=' such as "&&=&&&=&&&&==&===&===="), presence/absence of '=' per segment (key-only vs key=value), percent-encoded sequences including %0D/%0A combinations that interact with breakConversion, '+' characters, and the plusToSpace (URI_TRUE/URI_FALSE) and breakConversion (URI_BR_DONT_TOUCH, URI_BR_TO_LF, URI_BR_TO_CR, URI_BR_TO_CRLF) parameters exposed by the Ex/ExMm variants — URI_BR values and plusToSpace=URI_TRUE exercise the most branches in UnescapeInPlaceEx and should be preferred as the default/most permissive configuration. Also vary the UriMemoryManager passed to the ExMm variant (NULL for default libc manager vs a custom/failing one) to reach the malloc-failure cleanup branches in AppendQueryItem and DissectQueryMallocExMm.
This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests do with the target stays.
